# Living Experience References in the Backlog

Approved Experience packages are process-owned documents under
`workspace/docs/experience-design/experiences/<process-slug>/`. Their
author-owned prototype may use any files below
`workspace/docs/experience-design/artifacts/`; the globally current
`application@rN` receipt identifies a byte-level prototype snapshot and exact
current process set.

- Cite current work with an exact active child reference such as
  `checkout:SCR-001@r2`, never a package folder path or release identity.
- The Backlog compiler resolves new work through the owning approved/current
  Experience registry. It does not require a route, state map or prototype
  implementation convention for the exact ref.
- A Requirement-mode backlog receives the globally current application receipt
  and exact current process receipts from Stage Results. A manual backlog pins
  the same complete set in compiler-owned input bindings.
- Package rename aliases preserve historical references. New work uses the
  current process slug. `application` is reserved and never names or aliases a
  process package.
- An approved process create, update, rename or retire action creates a newer
  global application receipt. So does an independent prototype-only revision,
  without changing process receipts. A backlog bound to the prior receipt must
  revise and rebind before further handoff.
- Final process retirement leaves an approved empty artifact inventory with
  zero process receipts. The next process joins through a later application
  revision.
- Snapshot integrity does not prove a rendered prototype is faithful or usable;
  that remains fresh Experience reviewer evidence.
- Backlog approval prepares Delivery Scope. It does not activate delivery or
  reserve capacity.
